**Triage — objectui#8327 family (8 cards). `domain:spec` · `pm:queue`. ⛔ These are NOT decision-box cards, and the reason is a measurement, not a preference.**

Taken **2026-09-10T13:39Z** (clock read in the same call that posts this).

### The ruling that governs all eight

Every one of these cards offers a key three exits — *declare · retire the read · route to the producer*. ⭐ **That choice is not free, and for most keys it is already made by the contract.**

`packages/types` in this repo is a **mirror**, not an authority: `objectql.ts` re-exports from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`KanbanConfig`, `ListColumn`, `SelectionConfig`, `PaginationConfig`, …) and its own docblocks say so — *"Aligned with @objectstack/spec ListViewSchema.rowActions"*, *"DERIVED from the zod `ListViewSchema` … which itself derives from `@objectstack/spec/ui`"*. ⇒ declaring a key here that the platform contract does not declare makes this repo **accept what the platform refuses**. SKILL.md settles that direction outright:

> 协议为基准:spec 与代码不一致默认改代码对齐;改协议单独立卡,⛔ 不作缺陷卡的选项。

⇒ **The exit is determined per key by one question: does `@objectstack/spec` declare this key, and on which schema?**

- **declared in spec** ⇒ align the mirror. That is *restoring declared = enforced*, a named non-escalating class. Mechanical.
- **not declared in spec** ⇒ ⛔ "declare" is **off the table** on this card. The exit is retire-the-read or route-to-producer. Also mechanical.

Either way no maintainer ruling is owed, which is why all eight are `pm:queue` rather than `needs-user-decision`.

### The screening measurement — with both controls

Word-frequency over `packages/spec/src/ui/` on objectstack `origin/main`:

| key | hits | key | hits |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| `disabled` | 67 | `enforceFieldSecurity` | **0** |
| `recordIdField` | 9 | `redactFields` | **0** |
| `resultDialog` | 7 | `rowActionDefs` | **0** |
| `undoable` | 5 | `hideFields` | 19 |
| `allDayField` | 3 | `requiredPermissions` | 97 |
| `endDateField` | 20 | `rowActions` | 4 |
| `startDateField` | 52 | | |

⭐ **Controls, because a zero proves nothing on its own:** positive — `groupField` 7, `NavigationConfigSchema` 5, `KanbanConfigSchema` 8 (all non-zero, the corpus is being read); nonsense — `zzqx_no_such_key` **0**. ⇒ the three zeros above are readings.

⚠️ **What this screening does and does not establish.** A hit proves the token exists somewhere under `spec/src/ui/`; it does **NOT** prove the key is declared *on the schema this particular read's node maps to*. ⇒ a non-zero means "declare may be available, go confirm it on the right schema"; a **zero** is decisive the other way — the key is nowhere in the UI contract, so declaring it here would fork the contract. **Confirm each non-zero with the TypeScript checker on the actual declaring type** — the same instrument these cards already used (`checker.getPropertyOfType`), ⛔ never a grep (objectui#8410 is the standing card that grep-shaped absence claims are unsound).

## This card — `components`, 4 keys / 6 sites off `UIActionSchema`

All four screen **non-zero** in the UI contract (`disabled` 67 · `recordIdField` 9 · `resultDialog` 7 · `undoable` 5). ⇒ "declare" is plausibly available for each — **but confirm on the actual declaring type before writing anything**, because the screening cannot tell `disabled` on an action from `disabled` on some unrelated schema, and 67 hits is exactly the kind of number that invites a wrong assumption.

⇒ Per key: confirm against spec's action schema with the checker. Declared there ⇒ align the mirror. Absent there ⇒ retire the read or route to producer; ⛔ do not declare it here.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — the diff is small per key, the per-key confirmation is the work.

## ⛔ The scope and the decision rule are triage's, quoted rather than summarised

Triage comment [`5619607236`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8648#issuecomment-5619607236) settles the exit per key, and settles it **against** the card's own guess:

> ⇒ **The exit is determined per key by one question: does `@objectstack/spec` declare this key, and on which schema?**
> - **declared in spec** ⇒ align the mirror … Mechanical.
> - **not declared in spec** ⇒ ⛔ "declare" is **off the table** on this card. The exit is retire-the-read or route-to-producer. Also mechanical.
> Either way **no maintainer ruling is owed**, which is why all eight are `pm:queue` rather than `needs-user-decision`.

And its screening, with both controls, over `packages/spec/src/ui/` on objectstack `origin/main`: `disabled` **67** · `recordIdField` **9** · `resultDialog` **7** · `undoable` **5** — all four non-zero.

⚠️ Triage then says exactly what that screening does **not** establish, and this is the sentence to work from:

> A hit proves the token exists somewhere under `spec/src/ui/`; it does **NOT** prove the key is declared *on the schema this particular read's node maps to*. ⇒ a non-zero means "declare may be available, **go confirm it on the right schema**" … **Confirm each non-zero with the TypeScript checker on the actual declaring type** — ⛔ never a grep.

⭐ `disabled`'s 67 is singled out by triage as *"exactly the kind of number that invites a wrong assumption"*. Treat it as the most dangerous of the four, not the safest.

## The six sites, from the card

| file | keys (line of the first read, at the card's sha `154fe2a` — ⛔ re-derive) |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx` | `disabled` · `recordIdField` · `resultDialog` · `undoable` |
| `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-icon.tsx` | `disabled` · `resultDialog` |

Four distinct keys, six read sites, one declaring type (`UIActionSchema`). The card's evidence came from `checker.getPropertyOfType` on the static type of `schema` **before** the cast, so `BaseSchema`'s string index signature (objectui#5155) cannot mask a missing declaration. ⭐ Use that same instrument; ⛔ objectui#8410 is the standing card that grep-shaped absence claims are unsound.

## ⚠️ Pins that name this type — read them before you write

Measured by this seat on `origin/main` before dispatching: `UIActionSchema` appears in **8** test-tree files, three of them under `packages/types/src/__tests__/`:

- `action-callback-retired-7068.test.ts:82` — carries `'UIActionSchema (objectui#5934); a success notice is successMessage. Retired under ADR-0049 '`
- `component-docs-retired-handler-keys-7340.test.ts:347` — *"`UIActionSchema.onSuccess` is LIVE (the spec's navigation …)"*
- `content-channel-family-d-9256.test.ts:43` — names *"the `UIActionSchema` arm of `button`"*

⇒ as far as I read them, these pin **callback/handler** keys (`onSuccess` and the retired callback family) and **not** your four. ⛔ That is my reading, not a clearance: open all three and confirm per key before touching anything. A pin naming a key is a ruling in machine-readable form, and a card that walks into one gets vacated — this seat vacated objectui#9091 four hours ago for exactly that.

## ⚠️ My screening control was polluted, and I am telling you so you do not inherit it

I re-ran triage's nonsense control in **this** repo's test tree and `zzqx_no_such_key` returned **2 files**, not 0 — because two other tests use that exact token as *their* negative control (`detailRendererUndeclaredKeys-8649.test.ts:309`, `listViewNonAuthorKeys-8653.test.tsx:146`). A nonsense word reused enough times stops being nonsense. Clean replacements measured here: `qqzz_absent_token_9999` → 0, `NoSuchSchemaXyzzy` → 0. ⛔ Pick your own and verify it is zero **in the corpus you are about to search**, ⛔ never inherit one.

## `Clause-②: yes`, and why it is declared before the verdict is known

The card states it: ⛔ *"Declaring a key is a published-type widening on `@object-ui/types` ⇒ Clause ② applies to whatever lands, with `needs:contract-review` on card and PR."* Per-key the answer may turn out to be retire-or-route, which would not widen — but `references/contract-review.md:10` makes this declaration the **conservative direction** and ⛔ not a final finding. I have hung the carrier on this card and the PR must carry it. ⛔ **You hang no label, add none, remove none.**

⇒ If every key lands as retire-or-route and nothing widens, say so in the report; the seat re-reads the declaration against the diff at landing. ⛔ Do not re-declare it yourself.

## ⛔ What this card must not become — the card's own three fences

- ⛔ **Not rows in `undeclared-but-consumed-keys-6150.test.ts`.** objectui#8327's finding is that filing them there is a published-type widening wearing the costume of bookkeeping.
- ⛔ **Not folded into objectui#8347.**
- ⛔ Not one answer forced onto four keys. Say per key which of declare / retire-the-read / route-to-producer it is, and why, with the checker reading that decided it.

## Deliverable

Worktree → code → tests → changeset → push → **draft** PR carrying `needs:contract-review` (which I hung; you do not). ⛔ Do not flip ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — landing is the seat's.

Report structured JSON: PR number and head sha, the per-key verdict with the exact `checker.getPropertyOfType` reading behind it, every premise of mine and of the card confirmed **or refuted**, your firing controls including the negative one you chose and verified, and CI as total / success / skipped / non-green plus whether `total_count` equals the returned array length.

**Container hazards.** `/home/user/objectui` is SHALLOW with a STALE `origin/main`; `/home/user/objectstack` is a shared primary checkout — ⛔ never fetch, checkout or cut a worktree in either; clone fresh into your own scratchpad subdirectory. ⛔ No `git stash`, ⛔ no `git worktree prune`, ⛔ never kill by process name, ⛔ never mutate the shared `node_modules`. ⚠️ `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` is **not executable** — invoke as `bash <path>`; a direct call exits **126**, a reading about permissions and ⛔ not about anything you were measuring; ⛔ never `chmod` it. ⚠️ `vitest run --disable-console-intercept FILE` swallows the positional filter — use the `=` form under `timeout -s KILL`.

**Measurement discipline.** ⛔ `grep -c` counts lines, not occurrences. ⛔ A zero needs a same-subject control that fires. ⛔ A pathspec is not a corpus. ⛔ Never write "(no output above = clean)". ⛔ Never write a model identifier into any artifact.

⚠️ `Test (shard 1/4)` runs against a 20-minute ceiling; nine readings this shift span **661–1204 s**. A `cancelled` there is objectui#9499, ⛔ not your diff — report it and stop, ⛔ do not re-run it, ⛔ do not touch `timeout-minutes`.
